body.en: Under this method a fixed amount is charged as depreciation every year, so the book value falls in a *straight line* to the residual value at the end of the useful life. The rate is expressed as a percentage of the original cost. For an asset bought during the year, depreciation is charged only for the months it was used.

points.en: Annual depreciation = (Cost − Residual value) ÷ Useful life
Simple; asset can be written down to zero or scrap value
Burden on profit rises in later years as repairs increase

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Machinery bought on 1 April 2022 for ₹1,80,000; installation ₹20,000; residual value ₹10,000; useful life 5 years. Find annual depreciation by SLM, the rate, and the book value on 31 March 2025.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Machinery bought on 1 April 2022 for 1,80,000 rupees; installation 20,000 rupees; residual value 10,000 rupees; useful life 5 years. Find annual depreciation by SLM, the rate, and the book value on 31 March 2025.
Cost equals 1,80,000 plus 20,000 equals 2,00,000 rupees.
D equals (2,00,000 minus 10,000) divided by 5 equals 38,000 rupees per year.
Rate equals 38,000 divided by 2,00,000 times 100 equals 19 percent.
Three years to 31 March 2025: 3 times 38,000 equals 1,14,000. Book value equals 2,00,000 minus 1,14,000 equals 86,000 rupees.
So the answer is D equals 38,000 rupees p.a.; rate 19 percent; book value 86,000 rupees.
